requirements.text: Design Architecture Design Document defining 4-layer separation: Presentation (SwiftUI Views), Business Logic (Use Cases/Interactors), Domain (Entities/Models), and Infrastructure (Repositories/Services)
acceptance_criteria: Document clearly defines each layer's responsibilities
Layer dependencies flow inward only (Presentation → Business → Domain ← Infrastructure)
Explicit data flow patterns documented with diagrams
Swift 6.2 concurrency patterns specified for each layer

requirements.text: Create Boundary Contracts (protocols) for the Transcription layer enabling multiple backend implementations (MLX, WhisperKit, AssemblyAI, Parakeet)
acceptance_criteria: TranscriptionService protocol defines common interface for all backends
TranscriptionBackend protocol abstracts provider-specific implementations
Async/await signatures for all transcription operations
Error handling contract with domain-specific error types

requirements.text: Design Interface Definitions with complete method signatures for all layer-to-layer communication
acceptance_criteria: Protocol definitions include full method signatures with types
Associated types specified where needed
Async throws patterns for error propagation
Documentation comments for each method

requirements.text: Create Data Flow Diagrams showing how audio, transcription, and UI state flow through all layers
acceptance_criteria: Sequence diagrams for: Start Recording → Audio Capture → Transcription → UI Update
State transition diagrams for Session lifecycle
Data flow for Real-time streaming transcription
Error propagation paths documented

requirements.text: Design Dependency Injection Strategy for wiring layers together at runtime
acceptance_criteria: Composition Root pattern defined for app startup
Protocol-based injection (no concrete dependencies in upper layers)
Factory patterns for creating backend implementations
Test double injection strategy documented

requirements.text: Create Migration Strategy for moving from Big Ball of Mud to clean architecture incrementally
acceptance_criteria: Phase-by-phase migration plan with milestones
Strategy for extracting logic from NotesView (3713 lines) into layers
Strategy for SessionRepository (2147 lines) decomposition
Backward compatibility maintenance during migration
Feature flags or branching strategy for safe rollout

requirements.text: Design Domain layer entities and value objects for Meeting, Session, Transcript, and Utterance
acceptance_criteria: Immutable value objects for core domain concepts
Proper Swift value semantics (Equatable, Hashable, Codable)
No dependencies on UI or external frameworks
Domain logic isolated from infrastructure concerns

requirements.text: Create Risk Assessment with technical risks and mitigation strategies
acceptance_criteria: Performance impact analysis (layer overhead)
Memory management concerns with Swift 6.2 actors
Testing strategy for new architecture
Rollback plan if issues arise during migration

requirements.text: Design Business Logic layer with Use Cases for key operations (StartSession, GenerateNotes, ExportTranscript)
acceptance_criteria: Each use case is a single responsibility class
Use cases orchestrate domain entities and infrastructure services
Input/output boundaries defined as protocols
Async/await patterns for long-running operations

requirements.text: Define Infrastructure layer patterns for Storage, Audio, and AI Services
acceptance_criteria: Repository pattern for data persistence
Service pattern for external APIs (OpenRouter, Voyage, Ollama)
Audio capture abstraction over SystemAudioCapture and MicCapture
Backend-specific implementations conform to shared protocols

requirements.text: Document Swift 6.2 Concurrency patterns for thread-safe layer communication
acceptance_criteria: Actor isolation strategy for domain layer
Sendable conformance for data crossing boundaries
Structured concurrency patterns for use cases
AsyncSequence usage for streaming transcription

requirements.text: Create Acceptance Criteria for validating the design quality
acceptance_criteria: All layers have clear, documented responsibilities
No circular dependencies between layers
Domain layer has zero external dependencies
All public APIs are protocol-based
Design supports adding new transcription backend without touching UI
Unit testing is possible for each layer in isolation

risks.description: Migration complexity from 36K lines with massive view controllers could introduce bugs
risks.mitigation: Incremental migration with comprehensive tests at each phase; feature flags for gradual rollout

risks.description: Performance overhead from layered architecture affecting real-time transcription
risks.mitigation: Benchmark critical paths during design; maintain zero-copy data flow for audio; profile before/after

risks.description: Team learning curve for new architecture patterns may slow development
risks.mitigation: Document extensively; pair programming during transition; provide architecture decision records

risks.description: Swift 6.2 strict concurrency may require significant refactoring of existing async code
risks.mitigation: Design with StrictConcurrency=complete in mind; use actors for shared state; review Sendable conformance

risks.description: Dependency framework updates (MLX, WhisperKit) may break layer abstractions
risks.mitigation: Adapter pattern for external dependencies; semantic versioning discipline; abstraction layers over direct framework use

stakeholders.name: Lead Developer
stakeholders.concern: Maintainability and ability to test components in isolation

stakeholders.name: Product Owner
stakeholders.concern: Preserving existing functionality while improving architecture

stakeholders.name: End Users
stakeholders.concern: Stability and transcription accuracy must not degrade

stakeholders.name: Future Contributors
stakeholders.concern: Clear code organization and onboarding documentation

stakeholders.name: MLX/WhisperKit Integration
stakeholders.concern: Abstractions must not limit access to framework capabilities

competitive_signals: TCA (The Composable Architecture) provides excellent patterns for SwiftUI state management
Clean Swift Architecture emphasizes testability through protocol-based design
Apple's modern concurrency patterns (async/await, actors) should be foundation of layer communication
Repository pattern widely adopted for data layer abstraction in Swift apps
research_signals: Protocol-oriented programming is idiomatic Swift approach for dependency injection
Actor-based isolation is essential for thread safety in Swift 6.2
Use Case pattern effectively separates business logic from UI and infrastructure
Migration from monolithic to layered architecture should be incremental, not big-bang

boundary_contracts.description: Protocol definitions for all layer boundaries

dependency_injection_strategy.description: How layers will be wired together
